audit_question: Does prospective behavioral success justify interpreting the affine alpha as an identified prediction of a unique natural counterfactual carrier amplitude, rather than as a robust output control law?

near_collision_examples.interpretation: Nearly identical source margins can receive substantially different optima on the finite v10 grid, so the scalar feature does not identify a unique target-guided alpha. Grid discretization and broad behavioral plateaus are plausible contributors.

reason: The frozen rule is prospectively sufficient and selective, but equally good behavior under materially different alpha values means behavioral recovery alone does not identify a unique natural carrier gain or upstream computation.
next_action: Measure a preregistered affine-alpha dose response on the prospective lexicon. A sharp optimum supports calibrated gain; a broad plateau confirms robust-control rather than amplitude-identification semantics.
